This page sets the editing standards for everyone who writes on the SWCCG Wiki, human or AI. The same rules apply to all editors. The wiki is an encyclopedia: a compendium of existing knowledge that is honest about where the knowledge comes from. Editors do not invent knowledge. == Standing rule: SWCCG is a small world (identity matching) == '''Bill (2026-10-12; repeated many times):''' SWCCG is a small world. If a match is about '''99.8%''' likely to be the same person, treat them as one person and go with it. '''Never ask Bill to confirm near-certain matches.''' Skip only genuinely ambiguous cases. '''State near-certain matches plainly (Bill, 2026-10-13):''' once a match passes this rule, write it as fact. Do not add "(inferred)", "matched by name" or conflict/hedging notes on pages, tables or Talk pages. Keep factual spelling-variant notes (e.g. listed as "Clint Hayes"). This covers '''all''' identity matching: * '''Name variants:''' nickname or short form, middle initial, obvious typo, same events (Charlie/Charles, Matt/Matthew). * '''Nicknames and handles:''' forum shorthand (for example "BFred" for [[Brian Fred]]), and GEMP, Holotable, DeckTech, or Slack handles when context makes the match near-certain. * '''Photo identification:''' a tag or caption, the person's own comment, elimination within a tagged group, a nickname or handle plus thread or event context that makes the person near-certain, '''or''' a distinctive name plus a Decipher or SWCCG link (for example, a Decipher staffer of that name), with the reasoning on the page's Talk page (Bill, 2026-10-27). A photo may come from any source. Uncertain faces stay unidentified. * '''Exact name + Star Wars CCG Facebook group (Bill, 2026-10-30):''' an exact legal-name match already on the wiki who is a member of facebook.com/groups/starwarsccg is the same person; dest. Group membership is a Decipher/SWCCG link. Hometown match is extra color, not a gate. A public Intro with no SWCCG text does not block. Worked: [[John Petelle]]. Still skip locked identity traps and inexact names (Caputo ≠ Caputa). * '''Decklist and results attribution:''' last-name-only sheets, first name plus initial, Username boxes, and published nicknames — merge onto the identified player page when context makes the match about 99.8%. One canonical page per person; other names redirect. Link as [[Canonical|Name as in source]]. Add an "also known as" or handle note on the person page. '''Conflicting spellings.''' When name variants conflict, compare the sources (results, forums, decklists, videos) and use the best-supported name for the page; the other spellings are redirects, with a "sometimes spelled" note on the page. Example: [[JW Millet]] (also published as J.W. Miller and JD Millet). == Write for the reader == * '''Reader value decides what stays.''' Include a fact if it changes what a player understands or what a collector does. Cut it if it does not, even when it is true and sourced. Catalog bookkeeping, such as a rarity code or how an encyclopedia labels a pack slot, is not reader value. * '''Be concise.''' Use short, neutral sentences. Cut repetition and unnecessary detail. Cut words before facts. When a source has a long list, put it in one sentence and move on. Clarity and full understanding come first: a sentence or quote may be as long as clarity needs (Bill, 2026-10-26). * '''Describe the subject, not the sources.''' Write "X is Y", not "The Encyclopedia lists X as Y". Where the information came from belongs in the citation. * '''Minor facts are welcome.''' Many readers collect and never played, so short, sourced collector and pack facts, such as the original price of a pack, add to the article. * '''Give an example for an unusual rule.''' A concrete example makes a strange concept clear, for example "if both cards were in hand, they would be lost to [[Monnok]]". Not every rule needs one. * '''Lead with the fact (Bill, 2026-10-13).''' The first sentence says what the subject is and the most important thing about it. Context and background come after the facts, never before. * '''State facts plainly.''' When a reliable source, or Bill's own knowledge, supports a fact, state it directly ("Decipher showed Lucasfilm the card"). Do not soften it with "reportedly", "is said to", "appears to", or labels such as "soft" or "secondary". If a claim is genuinely disputed, name who says it ("According to Holland, ...") once, then move on. * '''No research notes in articles.''' The article body never contains process or meta text: no "research note", "this pass", "this page does not invent", "not found", "no source says", "unverified", and no Gaps, Open questions, Research, or Sources-checked sections. Open questions and empty searches go on the Talk page under Missing data. * '''Do not describe what an image shows.''' Captions identify the subject and credit the photographer ("Sealed first-series box. Photo: KaosBound."). Do not narrate visible content (art, colours, frames, which box is on the left). Quote printed text only when the text itself is the fact. * '''Captions don't say where a picture came from (Bill, 2026-11-04).''' Don't write "from LinkedIn", "his Facebook photo", "Photo: Reddit" or "Fair-use screenshot" in a caption, and don't put the source ref there. Just post the picture with its caption. The source, the Preserved copy and any fair-use note go on the File page. A photographer credit stays ("Photo: Decipher.", "Photo: teabo."). * '''Length discipline.''' Give readers enough sourced detail to understand the subject. Cover the people, chronology, relationships, features and concrete work that explain its significance. Add relevant detail when an article is too thin. Use prose for context and tables for catalogs or comparisons. Give each fact one clear home. * '''End directly.''' The last section ends on a fact, usually the outcome or the current state. No summary paragraph, no caveats, no "more research is needed". * '''One reference list.''' Use the References section only; do not add a separate Sources list that repeats it. * '''Filler check before saving.''' Search the body for "note", "research", "pass", "not found", "no source", "unverified", "soft", "reportedly", "appears", "Gaps", "Inferred". Rewrite each match as a plain fact or move it to the Talk page. "Inferred" is still allowed as a Talk-page or reference note (likely facts may be published marked inferred there); just do not put an "Inferred:" label in body prose. * '''Run the style lint (Bill, 2026-10-14).''' AI agents must run python3 authoring/style_lint.py draft.wiki --title "Page" (in the billbisco/swccg-wiki repo) and fix every flag before saving any article, then run style_lint.py "Page" on the live page after saving; never save with open flags. Human editors may run it too (optional). It flags hedge and meta words, Gaps/Notes/Research headings, a Sources heading outside deck and event pages, captions that describe the image, cited URLs without a Preserved copy, personal email addresses and empty refs, and reports the body word count against the previous revision. It has no sentence- or quote-length limit. == Cite your sources == * Important facts deserve a citation: numbers, dates, rules, and anything a reader might doubt. Not every sentence needs one. * When a fact is well established, add the reference and move on. * When a claim is disputed, doubtful, or an opinion, name the source in the sentence itself ("According to ..."). * '''Citation layout (Bill, 2026-10-20).''' Sources go in the References section as <ref> citations, each with its Wayback Machine Preserved copy inside the same ref: [https://example.com/page Title], site (date). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261020000000/https://example.com/page Internet Archive]. An External links section is only for further reading, and its links are archived too. Only deck and event pages (decklists, tournaments, championships, Retro League events) keep a Sources section; every other page cites in References. * '''Every cited URL needs a checked Wayback copy (Bill, 2026-10-20).''' Every external URL on a page needs a Preserved copy, including links in lists, tables, body text and External links. The copy is a Wayback Machine capture (web.archive.org/web/ + 14-digit timestamp + the URL) or an Internet Archive item. Cite a copy only after it has been opened and checked, or verified against the source by the archive worker. Links to wiki.swccg.com and swccg.com/images need no copy. * '''Private source documents (Bill, 2026-10-12).''' When Bill provides private source documents (for example, an organizer's email), host them under swccg.com/snapshots/ (for example, snapshots/email/) and archive them like any other source, with a Preserved copy. * '''No personal email addresses on wiki pages (Bill, 2026-10-14).''' Do not publish personal email addresses (player contacts, mailto strategy credits that only carry a private address, or emails embedded in Service rows). Keep callsigns, hometowns, dates, and citations. Drop an emptied email column. Exception: a clearly defunct, historically significant, non-personal address may stay (for example a Decipher corporate strategy credit such as joea@decipher.com). * '''Don't narrate source disagreements (Bill, 2026-10-13).''' When sources differ, state the best-supported fact and cite all the relevant sources on it. Explain the discrepancy on the Talk page, not in the article. Avoid sentences such as "Decipher announced 11 July; the Players Committee gives only Summer 2001." * '''Do not add inferences.''' If no source states it, it does not go in the article. Put the idea on the article's Talk page, labeled as an inference. == Accuracy == * Link card titles and use the exact card title, including the printing's own title (for example, the Alternate Image of [[Queen Amidala, Ruler Of Naboo]] is [[Queen Amidala, Ruler Of Naboo (AI)]]). * Give a price only where it shows something, such as an Alternate Image against the regular printing. A pack's original price is welcome. * Proofread and read the changes before saving. * '''Always give the deck's format (Bill, 2026-10-14).''' Every decklist page and table row names a format. If the source does not state it, use the smallest format that fits the newest set in the list and the date, and mark it "(from the card pool)". * '''Deck format comes from the tournament.''' A DeckTech post date does not determine a deck's format; use the tournament's format. For example, every FreedomCon 2001 deck is [[Premiere - Reflections III]]. == Holder and tenure tables == * '''No repeated person.''' Never repeat a person across rows when their tenure is continuous; show each name once on the row where they belong so one line shows their full tenure. * '''Merge identical adjacent rows.''' Merge adjacent rows with identical holders into one row with the combined date range. * '''Close gaps.''' Check for gaps between one holder's end and the next holder's start; research the true handoff date rather than leaving a gap. * '''One range, not capture dates.''' When nothing changed between documented dates, show one range from the start date to present (or to the last documented date if no longer current), not a list of capture dates. Never split a continuous tenure at a year or archive-snapshot boundary unless the role, team or title actually changed per a source. * '''Same role, one row.''' Abbreviations or wording variants of the same role (e.g. Dev = Developer) are one role: merge into one row with the full name. * '''Position first.''' In organization and roster lists, write every entry position first, then person (for example "Design Advocate: [[Chris Kelly]]"), including advocates, in the same format as team entries. Service roles inside teams (for example lead GEMP slicer) are positions too: write "Lead GEMP slicer: [[Jeremy DiPaolo]]", one sub-bullet per role, not "[[Jeremy DiPaolo]] (lead GEMP slicer)". == Photos of people == * '''Photo sources (Bill, 2026-10-27).''' A photograph of a person may come from any source. The only test is how certain it is that the photo shows the same person. * '''Small World Rule for photos (Bill, 2026-10-27).''' A distinctive name plus a Decipher or SWCCG link (for example, a Decipher staffer of that name) means the photo is taken as the same person. Record the reasoning on the page's Talk page. See [[#Standing rule: SWCCG is a small world (identity matching)|Standing rule]]. * '''Facebook photographs (Bill, 2026-10-30; worked: [[Charles Lund]]).''' Dest the photograph as the wiki File (lead and Photographs; caption is the name, or the words printed in the frame). Preserve a screenshot of the Facebook surface as it appeared (photo viewer or group post) as the Route C snapshot: a short yellow banner with the date and live URL, then that screenshot. File page: who, Facebook, date, live URL, Preserved copy. Identification stays on Talk. The Facebook-chrome screenshot stays off Photographs. * '''Photo difficulty is not a skip (Bill, 2026-10-30).''' Dest the best available photograph of the person. Tiny circulars, AVIFs, and low-resolution faces dest as JPEG; the wiki scales them. Worked: [[Jindrich Nepevny|Jindřich Nepevný]] 88×88 circular. Do not HOLD for a failed circular click, AVIF, "need a larger JPEG", or a two-person frame when the subject is identifiable. * '''Repeating face in a group (Bill, 2026-10-30).''' When one face is present across several pictures, dest that person (crop of that subject + uncropped original in Photographs). Worked: [[Roberto Borias]] left-most face. * '''Memes and logos are not the lead.''' Skip a meme, logo, or product circular as the person lead; dest a real photograph of the person from the same profile. Worked: [[David Shettlesworth]] fish photograph instead of the meme circular. * '''Identify from evidence under the small-world rule.''' Name a person from a tag or caption on the source (or the person's own comment), by elimination within a tagged group, '''or''' from a nickname or handle plus thread or event context that makes the match about 99.8% certain (see [[#Standing rule: SWCCG is a small world (identity matching)|Standing rule]]). Mark anything truly uncertain as unidentified rather than guessing. * '''No obscene gestures on person pages (Bill, 2026-10-12).''' Do not put a photo that shows an obscene gesture (for example a middle finger) on a person page. Such a photo may be used only as an identification reference; do not upload it to the person page or display it there. * '''Cite the source and an archive copy.''' On the File page, link the source photo or post and add a preserved copy (Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/... Internet Archive]). If no archive can capture it, say so. * '''Credit the photographer only when known.''' Otherwise leave the photographer field blank. A still from a video is credited to the video's creator (the Players Committee YouTube channel is titled Star Wars CCG; credit those stills Players Committee). * '''New file names only.''' Never overwrite an existing file; check for duplicates on the wiki first. * '''Hunt a lead photograph (Bill, 2026-10-16).''' When creating or expanding a person page, hunt a sourced photograph and put it on the page. Video stills from SWCCG shows are allowed; crop StreamYard nameplates, host picture-in-picture, letterbox, and empty background out of stills so a single subject is centered. Do not leave a person page without a photograph when a sourced copy exists. * '''One lead photograph.''' A person page carries one lead portrait at the top as [[File:Name.jpg|thumb|right|260px|Caption.]]. * '''Centered images of single subjects (Bill, 2026-10-16; restated 2026-10-17; measured 2026-10-17).''' A lead photograph of one person is cropped so the subject's head sits in the center of the frame. Measure the head bounding box on the original. The crop-box center must match the head center within 5% of the crop width. Crop letterbox, black bars, StreamYard chrome, empty background, other players, bags, and table until head and shoulders fill the frame (Shannon tightness: worked 230×208). After the crop, open the crop file; if you can name empty table, a bag, or another player on one side, recrop that side off. Worked: [[Kevin Shannon]] 2011 Match Play Championship crop. Worked miss: first [[Ray Bordier]] SAT crop (File:Ray Bordier DecipherCon 1999.jpg; face on the right, bag and other players on the left). If a hall-shot crop is still off after that gate, use the full original as the lead and keep the crop File on wiki unused. Worked: [[Aldrin Long]], [[Piergiulio Nardulli]], [[John Arendt]], [[Jason Burrows]], [[Stuart Jones]] (Bill 17 Oct 2026). * '''Additional photographs after the results (Bill, 2026-10-16).''' Extra photographs go in == Photographs == after Tournament Results, Retro League, Appearances, and In print when those sections exist, before Community card or See also. Use a <gallery> in that section. Do not put a gallery between the lead and the first heading. * '''Photographs extras are gallery thumbs.''' In == Photographs ==, extras use a <gallery> so they render as thumbnails. Do not put [[File:…|thumb|left|…]] or a raw File in that section: that floats a full-size picture. Worked miss: first dests of [[Allen Varney]] and [[Lester Smith]]. Worked: [[Michael Mikaelian]]. * '''Add good extras to Photographs (Bill, 2026-10-17).''' When a sourced photograph of a person is found, dest it. One lead; extras go in Photographs even when the page already has a portrait. Do not skip a good extra because a lead exists. Excess can be trimmed later. Worked: [[Gary Carman]] keeps sat14 as lead and the events-page sw99champ.jpg highlight in Photographs. * '''Every new photo goes in the gallery (Bill, 2026-10-27).''' Whenever a new photograph of a person is found, add it to the <gallery> in == Photographs == on that person's page, even when it is also the lead image. If the page has no Photographs section, add one in the usual place and keep the existing layout. Worked: [[Kendrick Summers]] (File:Kendrick Summers Rebel Leaders 1997.gif). * '''Keep the original with a crop (Bill, 2026-10-23).''' A person-page lead may be a crop of one subject from a larger still. Put the uncropped original in == Photographs == on the same page. Do not dest only the crop. A two-person or group original still belongs in Photographs when it is the source of the lead crop. Worked: [[Michael Mikaelian]] lead File:Michael Mikaelian 1996 Worlds.jpg with File:Michael Mikaelian at 1996 Worlds table.jpg in Photographs. * '''Heading is Photographs.''' Use == Photographs ==, not Gallery or Photos. == Pictures for articles == * '''Find pictures for every article (Bill, 2026-10-16).''' Event, place, set, mechanic, and website articles should carry relevant pictures when a sourced copy exists. Hunt for venue photographs, contemporaneous magazine coverage, player portraits from that event, product shots, related card images, and archived website graphics. * '''Historic venue photographs.''' Public-domain photographs of a venue used for an SWCCG event are allowed (worked: Cavalier Hotel for the [[1998 Decipher World Championship]] and [[1999 Decipher World Championship]]). * '''Venue photograph in the lead (Bill, 2026-10-16).''' An event article puts a photograph of the site in the lead. Two right-hand thumbs are allowed: the venue, and an event graphic or a later photograph of the same building. Worked: Cavalier Hotel on 1998 and 1999 Worlds; Virginia Beach oceanfront on [[FreedomCon]] and [[2001 Decipher World Championship]]. Hunt a contemporaneous licensed photograph first. * '''Website screenshots and original graphics (Bill, 2026-10-16).''' An article about a website carries archived screenshots or original site graphics of the home page and major section pages when those copies exist. Prefer the original GIF or JPEG from the archived site over a screenshot of Wayback chrome. Worked: [[Decipher.com]] lobby image-maps and section banners. * '''Split oversized website articles (Bill, 2026-10-16).''' When a website article is too large for one lead-plus-gallery, split major sections into subpages so each page can carry its own pictures. The hub keeps a short summary and a history gallery; the subpages hold the detail and the section graphics. Worked: [[Decipher.com]] into [[Decipher.com Star Wars CCG]], [[Decipher.com Galleries]], [[Decipher.com contests]] and [[Decipher.com downloads]]. * '''Straighten and crop.''' Straighten skewed scans so the subject fills the frame. Edit out magazine margins, adjacent cards, and card chrome from a portrait crop. * '''Two lead thumbs plus a gallery.''' Worked: [[Star Wars CCG Graded]]. * '''Person pages.''' Person-page photographs follow '''Photos of people''' (one lead thumb; extras in Photographs after the results). This section is for event, place, set, mechanic, and website articles. * '''Where to look first.''' For event, place, set, mechanic and website pictures, search SWCCG-associated sources first. Photos of people may come from any source (see '''Photos of people'''). * '''Convention and multi-game event pages (Bill, 2026-10-16).''' This is an SWCCG wiki. Worked: [[DecipherCon 2002]]. == Tournament and league pages == * '''All service goes in the Service table (Bill, 2026-10-14).''' Whenever a person page or a source mentions any service by that person, it must be a cited row in the person's == Service == table, not just prose. Service includes tournament director, judge, Squadron or other volunteer roles, Players Committee or Decipher roles, event host, and GEMP or development work. Each row gives the dates and the role in the source's own words, with a reference. If the page has no Service section, add one just above the first section. * '''Hosting a show is Service (Bill, 2026-10-16).''' Creating or hosting a published SWCCG show or channel is a Service row. Being a guest on someone else's show is Appearances. * '''Formats are single GEMP format names''', e.g. "Premiere - Jabba's Palace Sealed Deck" or "Premiere - Cloud City (Modified)". Link the exact format page if it exists; otherwise write the exact name as plain text. * '''Standings''': show the top 8, with the full list in a collapsed table (class="wikitable sortable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed"). * '''GEMP handles''' go in a standings column, filled where known from the player's page or the sources; leave the cell blank if unknown. * '''No handles in prose.''' Link the person; their page gives the handle. * '''Newest first (Bill, 2026-10-13).''' On player pages, Tournament Results and Retro League rows run newest first: latest year at the top, and within a year the latest event first (season standings and ROCS playoffs above that year's events). * '''Lead with the best result (Bill, 2026-10-13).''' A player page's lead opens with the player's best or most notable sourced result (a win, a top finish, or a season or ROCS title), not a weaker or older placement. Mention other results after it, keep it to a sentence or two, and cite it, reusing the result row's reference. * '''Every decklist page needs a source plus an archive copy (Bill, 2026-10-13).''' Cite where the list came from (the PC decklist page, a GEMP deck share, a forum post, or a Bill-provided email) under Sources, with a Wayback Preserved copy. Forum and PC pages are first saved as a snapshot under swccg.com/snapshots/, and that snapshot is archived; cite both the original and the archive. Never invent a source; if none can be found, say so on the Talk page. * '''Unmarked cards are the original (Bill, 2026-10-13).''' In a decklist, a card or objective not marked (V) is the regular Decipher card: link the original printing (for an objective, its two-sided page, e.g. [[Hunt Down And Destroy The Jedi / Their Fire Has Gone Out Of The Universe|Hunt Down And Destroy The Jedi]]). Link the (V) card only when the list says (V). If an objective is on the wrong side for the deck, it is a transcription error: leave the link and note it on the Talk page. == Tournament reports (Bill, 2026-10-24) == * '''One article per report.''' A player's own account of a tournament (from DeckTech, a fan site, the Players Committee forum, a video, …) gets its own article, titled '' (tournament report)''. It gives the author, publication, event, date, finish, record and decks, a table of the games described, and the original report. * '''The report text is reproduced verbatim and uncensored.''' Only a crude page title is replaced (by author and event); the original title stays in the article. * '''Every tournament a report mentions gets a page''' with what is known (date, site, format, players, winner, results) and a row on [[List of SWCCG tournaments]]. A side event covered in a report (for example a sealed event at Worlds) gets its own page and is mentioned on the main event's page. * '''Every named player gets an article''' about them and what they played, with a Tournament Results row citing the report. The small-world rule applies: a named person is the same person as the existing page of that name. A player named only by first name gets no page. * '''Reports update existing event pages:''' new participants, finishes, records, player counts, dates and sites, each cited to the report. * '''Discrepancies:''' Decipher's records, and an event page's existing sourced record, are trusted over a player's report until there is more evidence. The conflict is noted in a ''Discrepancies'' section on both the report article and the event page. * Each source has a catalog page (e.g. [[DeckTech tournament reports]]) and a category under [[:Category:Tournament reports]]; the overview is [[Tournament reports]]. == Appearances and In print == * '''Guest spots and written features (Bill, 2026-10-16).''' A guest on a video or audio SWCCG show, or the subject of a written feature, gets a cited row on their person page the same turn. The table is the mention, as with Service. * '''Appearances''' (video and audio guest spots): heading == Appearances ==, table columns Date / Outlet / Title / Role, oldest-first. Role in the source's own words, otherwise guest, co-host, panelist, or interviewee. Place after Tournament Results and Retro League (after Tournament Results when there is no Retro League; after Service or the lead when there are no results sections). * '''In print''' (written articles and features): heading == In print ==, columns Date / Publication / Title, oldest-first. After Appearances when both exist. * '''Cross-reference the host catalog.''' Filling a Guest(s) cell on a host page (for example [[BoardMatt]]) also adds the matching Appearances row on the guest's page that turn. * '''Interviews stay Interviews.''' == Interviews == with === Outlet, date === subsections remains the write-up of interviews OF the person when there are two or more. A video interview still gets an Appearances row. * '''Not every mention.''' The person must be a guest, interviewee, panelist, or named co-host who is there to discuss. Personal opinion lists are not cross-referenced. A first name with no last name stays unlinked (do not invent a person page). == Anagrams on person and card pages (Bill, 2026-10-15; restated 2026-10-17) == Sourced printed-title anagrams of a person, a close family member, or a named pet get their own section. Worked examples: [[Tom Braunlich]] / [[Nabrun Leids]]; family table: [[Chuck Kallenbach]]. * '''Person page.''' Heading is always == Anagrams ==. Place after the last career or results section, before See also. Use the same three-column table as [[Anagrams]] (Card / Unscrambled / Relation). The table is the mention; keep designer leads on the career. Stubs whose only sourced fact is the anagram keep one sentence in the lead and still use the table. * '''Intro sentence.''' Write the fact ("[[Nabrun Leids]] is an anagram of Braunlich" / "Printed titles scramble Braunlich's surname."), then the table. Cite [[Anagramed Decipherians]] and Encyclopedia 3.2 p.200 on that sentence. * '''Family and pets''' stay on the same table, with Relation filled in. Each related person still gets their own page and their own one-row table. * '''Only sourced rows.''' Copy Card / Unscrambled / Relation from [[Anagrams]] or a named Decipher source. Uncertain hub rows stay on the hub until the match is solid. Do not invent new anagrams. * '''Card page.''' Always Template:Card |anagram= ("The title is an anagram of [[Person]]."). That renders == Anagram ==. Not under Also known as. * '''Printed title.''' The Card column and the card page use the printed title. A short-title redirect is allowed ([[R'kik D'nec]] → [[R'kik D'nec, Hero Of The Dune Sea]]). * '''Hub.''' [[Anagrams]] is the full list. Person pages list only that person's rows. See also includes [[Anagrams]]. No card art on the person page. == Easter eggs on card pages (Bill, 2026-10-17) == Hidden jokes, call-outs, and extra images on a printing get their own section. Hub: [[Easter eggs]]. * '''Card page.''' One == Easter egg == via Template:Card |easter_egg=, immediately before See Also. Omit when none. Two eggs on one card stay one section. * '''Cite the fact.''' Cite Decipher Art Show 1999 (the capture you opened) as primary for Premiere through Jabba's Palace. Later-set eggs cite Encyclopedia 3.2. Write the fact, not the source. Zoom crop on the card. * '''Hub.''' [[Easter eggs]] is the full list. See also includes [[Easter eggs]]. * '''Packaging.''' The Hoth display-box egg goes on [[Hoth Limited]], same heading immediately before See also. == Card page titles (Bill, 2026-11-04) == One page per printing. Its title is the printed card title (no uniqueness dots), plus qualifiers only when another page would otherwise have the same title. Add them in this order: * '''(V)''' for every Players Committee virtual card, as printed. * '''Virtual printings:''' the current printing (the newest Virtual Modern set, or the only virtual printing) is plain '''Title (V)'''. An older virtual printing of the same card takes its set: ** Virtual Legacy: '''Title (V) (Virtual Block N)''', for example [[Well Guarded (V) (Virtual Block 8)]] next to [[Well Guarded (V)]] (Virtual Set 21). ** Virtual Original: '''Title (V) (Virtual Set N: Name)''', for example [[Hyperwave Scan (V) (Virtual Set 3: Revolution)]]. * '''Side:''' '''(Light)''' or '''(Dark)''' only when two cards with the same title are on opposite sides (for example [[Weather Vane]] and [[Weather Vane (Dark)]]). It is never used to tell two printings of one card apart. * '''Decipher set:''' '''(Set name)''' after the side when the side is still not enough (for example [[Sense (Dark) (Premiere)]] and [[Sense (Dark) (Coruscant)]]). * '''Printing marks''' last, as printed: (AI), (ALT), (Holo AI), (Errata), (PC Errata). Do not create numbered duplicates such as "(2)", and do not leave short-form alias redirects such as "Title (V) (Virtual Set 3)". Link the full title, piping the text if needed. Decklists link the printing that was legal on the event date (see [[#Tournament and league pages|Tournament and league pages]]). == Card versions vs products (Bill, 2026-11-10) == A '''version''' is the printed object. Two copies are the same version when language, border, '''set icon''' (Premiere has none), foil, printed game text and stats, and copyright year all match. A '''product''' is the box or pack. Leftover or repacked copies of the same version (Enhanced Premiere Unlimited boosters, First Anthology starters, Reflections I–III bulk non-foils) are extra products on that article. They do not get a new article or another title parenthesis. '''Named editions''' of one version that were independently sold as constructed sets share one article. The title stacks those edition names in chronological order, first product first. English white Premiere with no expansion icon and ©1995 that shipped in both Premiere Two-Player (February 1996) and Premiere Unlimited (April 1996): [[Imperial Barrier (Premiere Two-Player) (Unlimited)]]. Unlimited-only whites stay '''Title (Unlimited)'''. Two-Player exclusives and the Electrobinoculars / Lars' Moisture Farm misprints stay Two-Player-only titles. Premiere cards reprinted in the Empire Strikes Back Two-Player Game with ©1996: '''Title (ESB Two-Player)'''. Death Star II Starter reprints of earlier titles with ©2000 are their own version. The Players Committee lists revised wording on some of those reprints (Monnok, Grimtaash). They are not a third parenthesis on the 1995 white. Japanese black Premiere and Japanese white Two-Player are two versions because the border differs. Set hubs list every card the set contains and pipe the display name: [[Imperial Barrier (Premiere Two-Player) (Unlimited)|Imperial Barrier]]. Redirect the short names to the stacked title except where the short name is a different version (the Two-Player misprints). Infobox identity block, top to bottom: '''Set''' (primary product, first named edition). Then '''Set icon''' (printed expansion symbol, or none). Then '''Also in''' (other products of this version; omit when empty). Then Publisher, Era, and '''GEMP ID''' (first named edition first; two ids when two named editions). Gameplay '''Icons''' (Pilot, Warrior) stay with the face stats. GEMP: one wiki article and one uniqueness for one version. Two GEMP ids when that version is a named edition of two constructed sets (Premiere Two-Player first, then Unlimited). Leftover SKUs do not mint extra ids. A format can legalize Premiere Two-Player without Unlimited, and the reverse. swccg-guild/work#244. == Foreign-language card articles (Bill, 2026-11-05) == On English-language articles for a printing in another language, put a visible '''Title''' section near the top of the article body, before Card Text, showing the exact printed title in its original script. An infobox row is not enough. For Japanese printings, name the translation section '''Translation of Japanese Text'''. Place it below Lore and above Notes. Translate the title, lore and game text. '''Comparison with the English printing''' (Bill, 2026-11-08) is a short paragraph of real wording differences: a different number, actor, trigger, named card, or restriction. State the difference and stop. Do not restate the Title, Card text or Lore translations. Do not restate the English title. Omit the paragraph when the translations already cover the Japanese and the English is a straight counterpart. Do not add disclaimers such as "this comparison describes printed wording, not an official ruling". Worked: [[Han's Dice (Japanese)]] (ability 2 or more vs greater than 2; cancel and redraw vs draw another instead). [[Baniss Keeg (Japanese)]] (numbered options; 意識操作 for Alter). Worked miss: first [[Lateral Damage (Japanese)]] restamp restated both printings at length. == Card infobox Versions (Bill, 2026-10-26) == Template:Card '''Versions''' is the family navigator. Full lineage both directions. Omit the row when this printing is the only one. Dest remaining families in waves. Worked family: [[Luke Skywalker]]. * '''Closed prefixes''', oldest first: Decipher · Decipher (AI) · Decipher Errata · PC Errata · Virtual Original · Virtual Legacy · Virtual Legacy (AI) · Virtual Modern · Virtual Modern (ALT). * Unmarked '''Decipher''' is the printed face. Do not prefix Original. '''Title (Original)''' redirects to unmarked print. * '''Decipher Errata''' is a later Decipher rewrite (Glossary or Supplement). * '''PC Errata''' only when the Players Committee rewrote past Decipher. * '''GEMP ID''' is the id GEMP loads. Bare on the current playable article. Letter o on the first-published face. Letter d only as a middle layer when print, Decipher errata, and PC errata are three distinct texts. Worked: [[Luke Skywalker (Errata)]] is 1_19. * Current row: bold '''this page''' plus the GEMP id. * Host twins that share one GEMP id use one Versions line plus a hatnote "also listed as". * Fan and custom printings stay off championship Versions. * Docs: [[Template:Card/doc]] · [[Card versions]]. == Websites and sources == * '''Include the site's images (Bill, 2026-10-14; expanded 2026-10-16).''' An article about a website or source includes its relevant images (banners, deck or event graphics, home-page and section landing-page screenshots) from archived copies. Prefer original archived GIFs and JPEGs. Each File page cites the source page and a Wayback copy of the image or page. Event and mechanic articles follow '''Pictures for articles'''. * '''Official community links (Bill, 2026-11-07).''' Add an official site's useful public accounts and channels under External links, including Discord servers, social profiles and video channels. Verify each link against the site or another first-party source. Prefer the site's own permanent join or community URL when it redirects to a changing invite. Label the platform and follow the preservation rules. Keep citations in References. * '''Website logo (Bill, 2026-11-07).''' Give a website or organization its sourced, complete logo when available, including its identifying lettering. Use the original artwork in the lead or an infobox. A standalone icon or favicon can supplement the logo. A screenshot serves a separate purpose: show an interface, feature or historic version when it helps explain the subject. Each File page gives the source and a preserved copy. * '''Creator and contributor credits (Bill, 2026-11-07).''' Name the people or teams behind the project when the evidence identifies them. State their documented roles, what they contributed and when. Link existing wiki articles for those people or teams when applicable. * '''Game catalogs (Bill, 2026-11-07).''' When a site's game catalog is central to the article, list its documented games in a linked table or list. Distinguish featured games, playtests and independently hosted games as applicable. Reuse existing game articles. For missing titles, write a short sourced overview of the game and its connection to the site, with a reciprocal link. Keep the website article's Star Wars CCG coverage prominent. * '''Split for size and pictures (Bill, 2026-10-16).''' Oversized website articles split into pictured subpages. Each subpage gets its own lead image and gallery. == Articles about other card games == * '''Basic coverage (Bill, 2026-11-07).''' Include the game's original logo, publisher, credited designers when documented, a brief explanation of play, original release and supported production dates. Distinguish a final expansion from a documented end of production, and distinguish later editions, reprints and fan continuations. * '''Playable versions (Bill, 2026-11-07).''' Link directly to the game's playable destination on TCGMix or another documented service. Add the same destination to the service's game catalog. Archive each destination and verify its preserved content. * '''Game illustrations (Bill, 2026-11-07).''' Each game article includes the original game logo. An article about an online play service includes an actual gameplay image, showing Star Wars CCG when the service offers it. Individual game articles may also include a gameplay image where it helps explain the online version. Identify the game, edition and interface in the caption. Cite image sources on the File pages and preserve them. * '''SWCCG-first catalogs (Bill, 2026-11-07).''' Put Star Wars CCG first, followed by other Decipher games. Follow with other games, starting with the remaining Star Wars games and then the rest alphabetically. * '''Implementation details.''' Describe the supported card pool and available modes, such as bot play and multiplayer, where documented. Credit the people who develop the online implementation separately from the original game's publisher and designers. == Cross-linking checklist (Bill, 2026-10-14) == When you create a page, add it to every index it belongs in, and create missing pages for what it mentions: * '''Fan site:''' the [[Fan sites]] table and [[:Category:Fan sites]]. * '''Facebook group:''' the [[Fan sites]] table, [[:Category:Fan sites]], the admin's Service row, and a screenshot of the group. * '''Decklist:''' a page for every list an article mentions. Link it from the decklists index ([[Decklists]] or its source catalog), the event page, the player's Deck designs section and the source article. * '''Tournament:''' an article for every tournament mentioned, listed on [[List of SWCCG tournaments]], with a row in the TD's Service table. * '''Results, both ways (Bill, 2026-10-24):''' every player listed in an event's results has a row for that event in a results table on their own page (Tournament Results, or Retro League for league events), citing the same source. A link in See also or in a Tournament reports list does not count. A new player page always gets its results row, never an empty table. * '''People:''' named team members and organizers get player pages (stubs are fine), linked from the event and team. A personal opinion list (someone's Top 10) is not cross-referenced onto each named player's page. * '''Guests and features:''' guests on SWCCG video or audio shows, and subjects of written features, get a cited Appearances or In print row the same turn the host catalog records them. == Talk pages == Use an article's Talk page as the editors' notebook after any substantial edit. Useful sections are: * '''Missing data''': what you looked for and could not find or verify. * '''Possibly faulty data''': facts you doubt, with the conflicting sources. * '''Marginal cuts''': things you left out that another editor might want back, with their sources. * '''Build notes''': how a fact was traced, for the next editor. When tightening an article, move anything cut that may be useful (open questions, weak sources, cut text) to the Talk page under Missing data or Marginal cuts, so the article stays clean and nothing is lost. == Working together == * If you disagree with another editor's change, or think it is wrong or incomplete, say so and give your reason. * Once your concern has been heard and the decision stands, follow it. Speak up, then support the decision. * Check the current version of a page before editing, and apply your changes on top of other editors' wording rather than replacing it. * Use a short edit summary that says what changed. 戦士ではないキャラクター（ドロイドを除く）に配備すると、戦士技能［戦士アイコン］を与える。または戦士に配備すると、戦闘力＋１（「意識操作」カードの影響を受けない）。

帝国軍は高感度な器材を使用して、捕えた宇宙船の閉ざされた区画を探査する。探査部隊ＢＴ－445はミレニアム・ファルコン号を調べようとした。

'''Title:''' Scanning Crew. '''Card text:''' Use 1 Force to look at the opponent's hand for 10 seconds. '''Lore:''' The Imperial forces use highly sensitive equipment to scan closed compartments of captured starships. Scanning crew BT-445 tried to inspect the Millennium Falcon. '''Comparison with the English printing:''' The Japanese calls the destination the Used Deck, while the English calls it the Used Pile. The Japanese lore describes closed compartments rather than shielded compartments, and says that BT-445 tried to inspect the ship rather than planned to search it.[[:File:Premiere-D-scanningcrew.gif|Scanning Crew original English printed face]].

This is the documentation for [[Template:Card]], the card-page template. One page = one printing. Do '''not''' put empty errata sections on a card that was never errata'd. Optional '''card_status''' — a short status label for a printing that needs context outside the standard Decipher / Players Committee bands (for example, a cancelled design's community remaster). The label appears above the card template. Use only a sourced status; omit it for ordinary printings. Optional '''set_icon''' — printed expansion symbol. Always shown. Premiere = none (still shown). Pass none or a wikilink/file for the printed icon. Alias '''expansion_icon'''. When omitted, Premiere-family sets (Premiere Limited, Premiere Unlimited, Premiere Two-Player, Premiere Two-Player Introductory Game, Premiere, Japanese Premiere, Japanese Premiere Two-Player, ESB Two-Player) default to none; other sets show an empty cell until filled. Do not mass-restamp 24k articles. Optional '''also_in''' (alias '''products''') — leftover or extra products that shipped this same version (Enhanced Premiere boosters, First Anthology starters, Reflections I–III bulk). Named editions of the same cardboard stack in the article title instead. Omit when none. Optional '''publisher''' — publisher credited by the set article ([[Decipher]], [[Players Committee]], or a named person). Inherit from the set infobox. For a cancelled set, use its documented planned publisher; this does not imply that the cards were released. Renders after Also in when filled. Optional '''era''' — championship era hub: [[Decipher era]], [[Virtual Original]], [[Virtual Legacy]], or [[Virtual Modern]]. Renders after Publisher when filled. '''GEMP ID''' — the id GEMP actually loads, as set_card (for example 1220_51, 1_19). Bare on the current playable article, o on the first-published face, d only as a middle layer when print, Decipher errata, and PC errata are three distinct texts. Pass '''gemp_id''' or the older '''card_uid''' (alias). Optional '''gemp_id2''' — a second GEMP id when this version is a named edition of two constructed sets. Render both as adjacent spans, 2PG first ('''gemp_id''') then Unlimited ('''gemp_id2'''). Omit '''gemp_id2''' when empty. Worked: Imperial Barrier white 71_249 then 51_249. Shown in monospace. Dest keys such as pc|vbN|... belong in authoring JSON, not here. Infobox identity order: Set, Set icon, Also in, Publisher, Era, GEMP ID, then rarity/stats/gameplay Icons. Optional '''rarity''' and '''uniqueness''' — omit either field when the source does not establish it; no blank row is shown. Read uniqueness from the printed title marker: one bullet is Unique, no marker is Unrestricted, and multiple bullets use the corresponding Limited or Restricted value. For a combo, inspect the marker on both halves. If the title area is cropped or unreadable, omit uniqueness. Optional '''credits''' — count only the gold coin circles in the card’s bottom credit area, following the card’s orientation. The single gold badge beside the lore panel is not a credit. Show only positive Credits. Omit the parameter when there are no credit coins or the value is unknown; empty, null and zero values do not render a row. Keep confirmed zero distinct from unknown in the source-data ledger. Optional '''pc_alias''' — Players Committee GEMP alias (601_x / 501_x) when it differs from the GEMP ID. Optional '''slip''' — printed slip number on the virtual sheet (for example 51E). Data, not the id. '''Versions''' — family navigator (Option C, 26 October 2026; errata prefix 26 October 2026). Closed prefixes, oldest first: Decipher, Decipher (AI), Decipher Errata, PC Errata, Virtual Original, Virtual Legacy, Virtual Legacy (AI), Virtual Modern, Virtual Modern (ALT). Unmarked Decipher is the printed face. Decipher Errata is a later Decipher rewrite. PC Errata only when the Players Committee rewrote past Decipher. Full lineage both directions. Omit when this printing is the only one. Host twins that share one GEMP id use one line plus a hatnote. Pass '''versions''' or the older '''printings''' (alias). Bold the current-printing label and place its GEMP ID in . Worked: [[Luke Skywalker]]. Do not pass '''version_label'''. The old Version row (printed / virtual) is dropped. Era and Versions already mark Players Committee printings as Virtual Original, Virtual Legacy, or Virtual Modern. Optional '''version_code''' (Bill, 2026-11-08) — this page's errata version: <Issuer>-E<n>, where the issuer is D (Decipher) or PC (Players Committee) and n counts that card's published changes in date order, rephrases included (PC-E1, PC-E2…). Renders as '''Errata version''' above the Errata mark. Omit it on the original printed face, which has no code. It is our version id, not a printed stamp: the stamp printed on the card goes in '''errata_mark''' as printed (E1, D-E1). Page titles stay as in the Style guide: plain = original, then (Errata), (Errata 2), (Errata 3). Worked: [[Hindsight (V) (Errata)]] = PC-E1. Optional '''likeness''' — person whose face is on the card: a photographic model Decipher (or the Players Committee) cast, or the film portrayer of that character. Wiki-link the person page. Worked: [[Mara Jade, The Emperor's Hand]] → [[Shannon Baksa]]; [[Aurra Sing]] / [[Aurra Sing (AI)]] → [[Michonne Bourriague]]. Omit when the art is illustration, a starship/weapon, or a later virtual photograph that is not that person. Optional PC label fields (swccg-guild/work#100) — the small labels the Players Committee prints on a Virtual card, copied by bot from billbisco/swccg-gemp card_labels.json; correct them there, not here, or the next bot run puts the old value back. '''original_title''' — the black title strip at the bottom left (the title of the card this one was made from; on Virtual Legacy cards the slip title). '''original_title_italic''' — yes when the whole strip is italic, or the italic part (for example Executor). '''errata_mark''' — the errata stamp, bottom right (E1, D-E1). '''ai_mark''' — the alternate-image stamp as printed, (AI) or (ALT). '''concept_credit''' — the "Original concept by …" line. '''art_credit''' — the art credit printed beside the art ("Image courtesy of …"). '''dedication''' — an "In memory of …" line in the bottom bar. '''printed_label''' — any other small printed line (for example a contest name on the card's edge). '''copyright_line''' — the vertical copyright line beside the art, as printed (the standard "ARTWORK NEITHER AFFILIATED WITH NOR ENDORSED BY LUCASFILM LTD." too; Virtual Block lines are recorded only where legible). The '''Alternate-image stamp''' row shows the Players Committee logo printed beside (AI)/(ALT). Worked: [[Endless Legions]] (original title, concept and art credits); [[Executor: Control Station (V)]] (partly italic title, Decipher copyright line). All are omitted when the card doesn't print them. Optional '''reviews''' — published reviews of this card (fan-site or magazine), one bullet each: reviewer, outlet, date when known, rating if given, a short summary and a brief quote, cited with a carrying the Preserved copy (set '''has_refs'''). Renders as '''Reviews''' after Strategy. Omit when none. Worked: [[Chasm]] (Jeff Hansen, Neglected Card Series). Optional '''anagram''' — one sentence that the printed title is an anagram of a named person. Renders as '''Anagram'''. Adds [[:Category:Anagrams]]. Omit when none. Link [[Anagrams]] from See also. Worked: [[Nabrun Leids]] → [[Tom Braunlich]]. Optional '''joke''' — a joke in this printing's title, lore or game text, cited (or approved by Bill, with the approval on the card's Talk page). Renders as '''Joke''' directly after '''Anagram'''. Adds [[:Category:Jokes]]. Omit when none. Link [[Jokes]] from See also. Worked: [[Swing-And-A-Miss]]. Optional '''easter_egg''' — the hidden picture, icon, likeness or other visual detail on this printing, cited. Renders as '''Easter egg''' immediately before See Also. Adds [[:Category:Easter eggs]]. Omit when none. Link [[Easter eggs]] from See also. Worked: [[Death Star: Trench]]. '''sources''' — card-data sources supplied here (card list, slip, PDF). Give each source its own bullet with a Preserved copy. The template renders a '''Sources''' heading only when filled. Do not repeat a source already cited with for one claim. List it here again only when it supplies the entire card entry. '''has_refs''' — set when the page has notes; renders '''References'''. '''see_also''' renders '''See Also''' only when filled. Optional '''image2''' — second portrait under '''image''' (same 280px width). Used for Objective 0/7 faces; omit on single-face cards. Optional '''image2_trim''' — display-only trim for excess padding on the second image. A value of 20 requests a 320px thumbnail and hides 20px on each edge inside a 280px-wide rounded window. Measure each image separately and preserve a normal black border, all text and all symbols. The source File and downloaded image are unchanged. Omit for ordinary images. Optional '''image2_layout''' — how to place '''image2''' when set: * omit or '''stack''' — force stacked vertically (0 on top, 7 below); default when unset * '''right''' — force side-by-side always (0 left, 7 right); classes '''card-portraits-row''' + '''card-rail-dual''' * '''responsive''' — preferred Objective mode: wide viewport = side-by-side (0 left, 7 right); narrow viewport (max-width '''720px''') = stacked. Same row/dual markup plus '''card-rail-responsive''' / '''card-portraits-responsive''' so CSS media query can adapt. Optional '''image3''', '''image4''', '''image5''', '''image6''' — further portraits, each 280px wide, with matching '''image3_trim''' … '''image6_trim''' (same rule as '''image2_trim'''). Used for the printed slip on [[Virtual Legacy]] card pages (swccg-guild/work#156), as '''image2''' shows the slip on [[Virtual Original]] pages. * Stacked layout (no '''image2_layout'''): they follow '''image2''' in order, top to bottom. A single-face card whose '''image2''' is free puts its slip in '''image2'''; a card whose '''image2''' is taken puts the slip in '''image3''' (a slip printed in two halves uses the next free slots, top half first). * '''right''' / '''responsive''' layout (two-sided Objectives): when '''image3''' or '''image4''' is set the portraits form two columns. The left column is '''image''' (0 side), '''image3''', '''image5'''; the right column is '''image2''' (7 side), '''image4''', '''image6'''. Put the 0 side's slip in '''image3''' and the 7 side's in '''image4'''; when a side's slip is printed in two halves, its second half goes in '''image5''' (0 side) or '''image6''' (7 side). In narrow (responsive) view the left column stacks above the right. Without '''image3'''/'''image4''' the layout is unchanged.

It shows a ''Blanked'' row after ''Era'' and adds [[:Category:Blanked cards]]. Blanking is not a new version: the card stays in its set and is legal in period formats before that date. Card Text

自分の地雷敷設ドロイドがいる位置カードの相手の側に配備する。次の自分のターンに「爆発」する。運命数を引く。そこにいる相手のキャラクターが運命数の数だけ即座にロストする（誰をロストするかは敵が選べる）。その時点でタイマー地雷もロストする。

Lore

''地雷敷設用ドロイドによって仕掛けられる時限式の爆弾。鉱脈やスパイス鉱山の爆破用に開発されたが、軍用に改造されている。''

Developed for blasting ore veins and spice mines, it has been modified for military use. '''Comparison with the English printing:''' The Japanese says to deploy at a location card and that the mine explodes on your next turn. The English specifies a site and the beginning of your next turn. The Japanese says the opponent chooses the characters lost; the English says their owner chooses.

相手の支配フェイズ、５フォース以上の消耗を受け、なおかつ、場に自分のドロイドがいる場合に、１フォース消費して使用できる。運命数を引く。その数の分だけロストデッキからランダムに選んで再使用してよい。

''ドロイドにとって、“創りしもの”への情熱は、神や宗教に匹敵する存在である。Ｃ－３ＰＯは、待望のオイルバスにありついた時、このフレーズを使った。''

'''Title:''' Thank the Maker. '''Card text:''' During the opponent's control phase, if you have suffered a drain of 5 or more Force. Have your droid on the table, you may spend 1 Force to use this. Draw destiny. You may randomly select that number from the Lost Pile and reuse them. '''Lore:''' For droids, devotion to ‘the one who creates’ is comparable to God or religion. ルークと能力値＞2の帝国軍が同じ戦闘に参加していれば使用できる。戦闘運命数を1回引いて加える（相手がベイダーなら2回）。[[:File:Japanese-Premiere-1301-116o-Video.jpg|Original Japanese printed face]].

'''Comparison with the English printing:''' The Japanese adds two destiny if the opponent is Vader; the English does so if the Imperial is Vader.

'''Lore:''' Vader and Obi-Wan Kenobi fought their final lightsaber duel near Death Star Hangar Bay 327. “I left you before my training was complete, but now I have mastered everything.”

任意の男性キャラクターに配備する。場に出ている女性キャラクターを1人、目標とする。目標は戦闘力－2。目標と同じ場所にいることになったら、ウーティーニー・エフェクトはキャンセルする。[[:File:Japanese-Hoth-This-Is-Just-Wrong-PSA-84363897.jpg|Original Japanese printed face]].

Cancel the Utinni Effect when it is at the same place as the target. '''Lore:''' “How could you think that? You apparently don’t know much about women.” '''Comparison with the English printing:''' The Japanese uses the wording 同じ場所 (same place).

'''Tauntaun Bones''' is a [[Light]] [[Effect]] from [[Hoth (Japanese)|Hoth (Japanese)]].

Title

トーントーンの骨

Card Text

1フォース消費して場に配備する。相手が運命数を引くごとに、その値に応じて以下の指示に従う。0：ユーズドデッキの一番上のカードを手札に加える。2：1フォース失う。2：1フォース起動する。3：このエフェクトをロストする。4：ロストデッキの一番上のカードを再使用する。5：キャラクターを1人、フォース消費なしで配備する。6+：なにもなし。[[:File:Japanese-Hoth-Tauntaun-Bones-PSA-170462293.jpg|Original Japanese printed face]].

Lore

''トーントーンの骨は死と生を共に表している。獲物の死と捕食者の生である。世の万物にまつわるフォースの満ち引きを象徴する。''

Translation of Japanese Text

'''Title:''' Tauntaun Bones. '''Card text:''' Use 1 Force to deploy on table. Each time the opponent draws destiny, follow these instructions by that value. Zero: Take the top Used Pile card into hand. Two: Lose 1 Force. Two again: Activate 1 Force. Three: Lose this Effect. Four: Retrieve the top Lost Pile card. Five: Deploy one character without spending Force. Six or more: Nothing. '''Lore:''' The bones of a tauntaun represent both death and life. They are the death of the prey and the life of the predator. They symbolize the ebb and flow of the Force in all things. '''Comparison with the English printing:''' Printed subtype is エフェクト.

Notes

Japanese-language printing of [[Tauntaun Bones]] in [[Hoth (Japanese)]].[https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf SWCCG Collecting Encyclopedia 3.2], pp. 43, 103. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008192828/https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf Internet Archive].

Title

トーントーン使い

Card Text

騎乗する乗用生物の戦闘力に2を加える。トーントーンに乗っているなら、戦闘運命数を引けない場合に1枚引ける。[[:File:Japanese-Hoth-Tauntaun-Handler-PSA-159563453.jpg|Original Japanese printed face]].

''コーマン・クィエンはエコー基地の偵察兵の典型と言える。野生のトーントーンを捕まえ、手なずけ、訓練を行うのだ。''

Translation of Japanese Text

'''Title:''' Tauntaun Handler. '''Card text:''' Adds 2 to the power of a creature vehicle he rides. If riding a tauntaun, he may draw 1 battle destiny if not able to otherwise. '''Lore:''' Corman Quien can be called a typical Echo Base scout. He captures, tames, and trains wild tauntauns. '''Comparison with the English printing:''' Game text uses 騎乗する (rides) for creature vehicles, not “drives.” Lore is present tense and specifies wild tauntauns.

'''That's It, The Rebels Are There!''' is a [[Dark]] [[Interrupt]] from [[Hoth (Japanese)|Hoth (Japanese)]].

Title

間違いない、反乱軍の秘密基地だ！

Card Text

自分の支配フェイズに自分の宇宙船を1隻、通常どおりにフォースを消費して、自分のプローブ・ドロイドがいる位置と同じ星系に移動させる。ただし航行速度で到達できる場合に限る。その宇宙船はそのターンにはもはや移動することはできない。[[:File:Japanese-Hoth-Thats-It-The-Rebels-Are-There-PSA-151452828.jpg|Original Japanese printed face]].

Lore

''「この星系だ。間違いなくスカイウォーカーも一緒に居る」''

Translation of Japanese Text

'''Title:''' That's It, The Rebels Are There!. '''Card text:''' During your control phase, move one of your starships, spending Force as usual, to the same system as a location where you have a Probe Droid. Only if it can be reached by hyperspeed. That starship can no longer move this turn. '''Lore:''' This is the system. Skywalker is certainly with them as well. '''Comparison with the English printing:''' Movement is to the system matching the Probe Droid’s 位置, limited by 航行速度, not “if within range.”

Notes

'''The First Transport Is Away!''' is a [[Light]] [[Effect]] ([[Utinni Effect]]) from [[Hoth (Japanese)|Hoth (Japanese)]].

Title

最初の輸送艇が突破しました！

Card Text

任意の星系上（ホス以外）に配備する。ホスの位置にいる任意の中型輸送艇を目標とする。目標がウーティーニ・エフェクトに到達したら、Xフォースを再使用する。X＝乗客の人数の2倍である。ウーティーニ・エフェクトをホス星系に移動する。ホスの位置カードでの戦闘時に自分の合計戦闘力に＋2される。[[:File:Japanese-Hoth-The-First-Transport-Is-Away-PSA-148375110.jpg|Original Japanese printed face]].

Lore

''「エネルギー・シールドを抜けたら、真っ直ぐランデブー・ポイントに向かいなさい。いいわね？ 幸運を祈ってるわ」''

Translation of Japanese Text

'''Title:''' The First Transport Is Away!. '''Card text:''' Deploy on any system except Hoth. Target any Medium Transport at a Hoth location. When the target reaches this Utinni Effect, retrieve X Force. X is twice the number of passengers. Relocate the Utinni Effect to the Hoth system. Your total power is +2 in battles at Hoth location cards. '''Lore:''' Once you have passed through the energy shield, proceed straight to the rendezvous point. All right? I'm wishing you luck. '''Comparison with the English printing:''' The power bonus is at ホスの位置カード, not “Hoth sites.” Lore uses いいわね？ instead of “Understood?”

The shield doors must close now. '''Comparison with the English printing:''' Printed subtype is エフェクト.

Title

触手

Card Text

相手がインタラプトを使用した直後に、1フォースを使用して場に配備する。そのインタラプトは通常通りの効果を及ぼすが、その後で触手に“巻きつかれる”（その場に置かれ、ゲームからは除外される）。同じ名前のインタラプトは今後すべて単一（＊）カードとなる。このエフェクトは「コントロール」の影響を受けない。[[:File:Japanese-ANH-Tentacle-SWCA-67795.jpg|Original Japanese printed face]].

Lore

''ダイアノーガは7本の触手を使って獲物を探し、捕える。幸運にもこの攻撃を生き延びた者たちによれば、この触手は水圧クランプなみの怪力を持っているという。''

Translation of Japanese Text

'''Title:''' Tentacle. '''Card text:''' Just after the opponent plays an Interrupt, use 1 Force to deploy on table. That Interrupt still has its usual effect, then is entwined by the tentacle. It is placed here and removed from the game. All Interrupts of the same name become unique cards. This Effect is not affected by Control. '''Lore:''' A dianoga uses its seven tentacles to find and catch prey. Survivors of such attacks say a tentacle has the monstrous strength of a hydro-clamp. '''Comparison with the English printing:''' Printed subtype is 即効エフェクト.

'''The Circle Is Now Complete''' is a [[Dark]] [[Interrupt]] from [[Reflections III: A Collector's Bounty|Reflections III: A Collector's Bounty]].

Title

いよいよ決着をつける時が来た

Card Text

ベイダーとオビ＝ワンが同じ位置カード上にいる時に使う。1フォース消費して決闘を行う。ライト・セーバーを持っているジェダイは戦闘値が＋2される。敗者は除外カードとなり、残りのゲームの間、同じ人物を表すカードは配備できなくなる。

Lore

''ベイダーとオビ＝ワン・ケノービは、デス・スターのハンガー・ベイ327付近にてライトセーバーで最期の決闘を行った。「修行半ばで貴様の下を去ったが、今やすべてを極めた。」''

Translation of Japanese Text

'''Title:''' The Time Has Finally Come to Settle This. '''Card text:''' Use when Vader and Obi-Wan are at the same site. Use 1 Force to duel. A Jedi with a lightsaber adds 2 to their duel total. The loser is placed out of play, and cards representing the same person cannot deploy for the rest of the game. '''Lore:''' Vader and Obi-Wan Kenobi fought their final lightsaber duel near Death Star Hangar Bay 327. “I left you before my training was complete, but now I have mastered everything.” '''Comparison with the English printing:''' The Japanese title paraphrases the English title as the time to settle the matter.

Notes

'''The Circle Is Now Complete (Japanese Reflections III Foil)''' is a Japanese-language foil printing of [[The Circle Is Now Complete|The Circle Is Now Complete]]. [[Decipher]] released it in [[Reflections III: A Collector's Bounty]] in October 2001. The ordinary Japanese expansion printing is [[The Circle Is Now Complete (Japanese)]]. Complete Card List v4 lists checklist R41 at rarity VR. Collector R-numbers are checklist references, not GEMP blueprint IDs.[https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/swccgcardlist4.0.pdf Star Wars Customizable Card Game Complete Card List v4.0], p. 31, Reflections III foil cards, R41. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261009184033/https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/swccgcardlist4.0.pdf Internet Archive].[https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf SWCCG Collecting Encyclopedia 3.2], p. 22. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008192828/https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf Internet Archive].[[:File:Japanese-The-Circle-Is-Now-Complete-Reflections-III-Foil-SWCA.jpg|Original Japanese foil face]]. Photograph by Duncan Jenkins.

See Also

* [[Translations of SWCCG#Japanese foils|Japanese foils]]

Card Text

自分の地雷敷設ドロイドがいる位置カードの相手の側に配備する。次の自分のターンに「爆発」する。運命数を引く。そこにいる相手のキャラクターが運命数の数だけ即座にロストする（誰をロストするかは敵が選べる）。その時点でタイマー地雷もロストする。[[:File:Japanese-ESB-Two-Player-Timer-Mine-Dark-SWCA-100703.jpg|Original Japanese printed face]].

''地雷敷設用ドロイドによって仕掛けられる時限式の爆弾。鉱脈やスパイス鉱山の爆破用に開発されたが、軍用に改造されている。''

'''Title:''' Timer Mine (Dark). '''Card text:''' Deploy on the opponent's side of a location card where one of your mine-laying droids is present. It "explodes" on your next turn. Draw destiny. '''Comparison with the English printing:''' The Japanese deploys at a location card and explodes on your next turn.

Title

タスケン呼吸マスク

Card Text

タトゥイーンの位置カードで、戦闘に勝利した時に、その場所に配備する。タトゥイーン上にいないキャラクターを対象にする。対象が到着したら、マスクを手に入れたことになる。タトゥイーンにいる間、対象の戦闘力と没収値は＋2、さらに耐：損耗<3を得る。

Lore

サンド・ピープルは、特殊なマスクを着用し、暑く不快なタトゥイーンの環境に散在した水分を回収している。吹き込む砂を取り除き、過剰な熱を発散させて体を守る働きがある。

Translation of Japanese Text

'''Title:''' Tusken Breathing Mask. '''Card text:''' When you win a battle at a Tatooine location card, deploy at that location. Target a character not on Tatooine. When the target arrives, it has obtained the mask. While on Tatooine, the target's power and forfeit are increased by 2, and it also gains immunity to attrition less than 3. '''Lore:''' Sand People wear special masks to recover moisture scattered in Tatooine's hot, unpleasant environment. They protect the body by removing blowing sand and dispersing excess heat. '''Comparison with the English printing:''' The Japanese grants immunity to attrition less than 3; the English grants immunity to attrition of exactly 3. The Japanese says to target a character not on Tatooine, without the English restriction “one of your characters.” The Japanese uses location card where the English specifies a site. The Japanese lore describes moisture in the environment, rather than the English “exhaled moisture.”[[:File:Premiere-L-tuskenbreathmask.gif|Tusken Breath Mask original English printed face]].

1フォース消費して、場の自分の側に配備する。自分のコントロールフェイズの間、好きなカードを手札からユーズドデッキの一番上へ戻してよい。

熟練した発進誘導員は、自動発進システムよりも早く宇宙船の発進準備を整える。帝国軍の攻撃時には、反乱軍基地から戦闘機が迅速に緊急発進する。

'''Vehicle Mine (Dark)''' is a [[Dark]] [[Weapon]] ([[Automated Weapon]]) from [[Hoth (Japanese)|Hoth (Japanese)]].

Title

対ビークル地雷

Card Text

自分の地雷敷設ドロイドの1体と同じ屋外の位置に配備する。宇宙戦闘機か生物以外のビークルがその位置に配備されるか移動してきた場合、あるいはその位置を通過した場合に“爆発”する。運命数を引く。運命数＋2＞装甲値か回避値なら、ビークルはロストする。運命数＞3なら宇宙戦闘機はロストする。対ビークル地雷もロストする。[[:File:Japanese-Hoth-Vehicle-Mine-Dark-PSA-159563449.jpg|Original Japanese printed face]].

Lore

''附近を通過する金属塊や接近するスピーダーのリパルサーリフト・フィールドに反応して射出され、爆発する。榴散弾はどんなに素早い機体でもかわすことができない。''

Translation of Japanese Text

'''Title:''' Vehicle Mine (Dark). '''Card text:''' Deploy at the same exterior location as one of your mining droids. It explodes if a starfighter or non-creature vehicle deploys, moves to, or passes that location. Draw destiny. The vehicle is lost if destiny plus 2 exceeds armor or maneuver. The starfighter is lost if destiny exceeds 3. The Vehicle Mine is also lost. '''Lore:''' It launches and explodes in response to a passing metallic mass or an approaching speeder's repulsorlift field. Even the quickest craft cannot dodge the shrapnel. '''Comparison with the English printing:''' Game text uses 位置 for site, 地雷敷設ドロイド for mining droids, and the Japanese title in the last sentence.

タトゥイーンにいるなら、「地元のいざこざ」と「ドロイドです！」をユーズド・インタラプトとして使用できる。フェルスのいる場所で「同士撃ち」を使用したなら、敵は自由に目標を選択することができる。[[:File:Japanese-ANH-Trooper-Davin-Felth-PSA-89673868.jpg|Original Japanese printed face]].

敵の側に潜伏中のスパイとして配備する。通常のスパイと異なり、位置カードでの戦闘中には、U-3PO戦闘力をライトサイドの合計に加える。スパイが"正体を現す"こととなったら、上記のカードルールはキャンセルされ、ライトサイドはこのドロイドを"盗んだ"場合と同様に使用できる。[[:File:Japanese-ANH-U-3PO-Yoo-Threepio-PSA-89673869.jpg|Original Japanese printed face]].

''オルデランの外交団に仕えていた通訳ドロイド。帝国軍がプログラムを改変し、諜報活動に使っていた。ドロイドは自分でも知らぬ間に帝国軍のスパイとなっていたのだ。''

Unlike ordinary spies, during battle at a location card, add U-3PO's power to the Light Side total. If the spy's identity is revealed, the above card rules are canceled, and the Light Side may use this droid as if stolen. '''Lore:''' This protocol droid served Alderaan's diplomatic corps. The Empire altered its programming and used it for espionage. The droid became an Imperial spy without even knowing it. '''Comparison with the English printing:''' The Japanese face uses the Light Side character template.

Title

ワイオスリー

Card Text

自分の支配フェイズの間、１フォース消費して、同じ位置カードにいる相手のビークルまたはドロイドを対象にして“購入”してよい。運命数を引く。運命数＞対象の運命数ならば、対象の配備コストと等しいフォースを“支払って”（消費して）、その対象を手にいれる。

Lore

''ルークのランドスピーダーを買ったスペースポート・スピーダーズのヴーヴリアン女性。ジャバ・ザ・ハットに1000クレジットの借金があるギャンブラー。多くの言語を話す。''

Translation of Japanese Text

'''Title:''' Wioslea. '''Card text:''' During your control phase, you may spend 1 Force to target an opponent's vehicle or droid at the same location card for ‘purchase.’ Draw destiny. If it is greater than the target's destiny number, ‘pay’ (spend) Force equal to the target's deploy cost and obtain that target. '''Lore:''' A Vuvrian woman of Spaceport Speeders who bought Luke's landspeeder. A gambler who owes Jabba the Hutt 1,000 credits. Speaks many languages. '''Comparison with the English printing:''' The Japanese calls the amount owed a debt; the English identifies it as a wagering debt. The Japanese describes obtaining the target after paying its deploy cost; the English says to take the target.

Notes

Japanese-language printing of [[Wioslea]] in [[Premiere (Japanese)]].[https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf SWCCG Collecting Encyclopedia 3.2], p. 97. 戦士の勇気

位置カードでの戦闘で、任意の戦士が単独で防衛している場合、戦闘運命数を１回余分に引ける。または、位置カードでの戦闘で、レイアが単独で防衛している場合、戦闘運命数を２回余分に引ける。[[:File:Japanese-Premiere-1301-119o-Face.jpg|Original Japanese printed face]].

''反乱軍兵士はみな、反乱同盟軍の自由の理想を心から信じ、勇敢に戦う。勇猛で機転の利く反乱軍は、しばしば帝国軍の軍勢を打ち負かしている。''

'''Title:''' Warrior's Courage. '''Card text:''' In a battle at a site, if any warrior is defending alone, you may draw one extra battle destiny. Or, if Leia is defending alone at a site, you may draw two extra battle destinies. '''Lore:''' Rebel soldiers fight bravely out of a sincere belief in the Alliance's ideal of freedom. Brave and resourceful Rebels often defeat Imperial forces.

Title

もうだめだ！

Card Text

ライフフォースが１５より小さいときの相手の支配フェイズに使用できる。場に出す。このターンの残りの間、フォースを失う毎に、失うフォースの数を半分にする（端数切り上げ）。Ｒ２－Ｄ２かＣ－３ＰＯが場に出ていれば、端数切り捨て。[[:File:Japanese-Premiere-1301-120o-Face.jpg|Original Japanese printed face]].

Lore

''３ＰＯは、数多くの災難に脅かされ、たびたび作動停止の危機に見舞われた。この不運な通訳ドロイドは、罪のない皮肉感覚が発達し、状況判断力も鋭くなった。''

Translation of Japanese Text

'''Title:''' All Is Lost! '''Card text:''' During your opponent's control phase, you may play this on table if your Life Force is below 15. For the rest of the turn, halve each Force loss, rounding up. If R2-D2 or C-3PO is on table, round down instead. '''Lore:''' 3PO has been threatened by many calamities and repeatedly faced shutdown. The unfortunate protocol droid developed an innocent sense of irony and a sharp eye for assessing situations.

'''Card text:''' Choose one. 1: Cancel I'm On The Leader (not affected by Sense). 2: Use 1 Force to move one TIE at Death Star: Trench to the Death Star system card (it moves for free). Also, if the lead starfighter is piloted by its matching pilot, you may add 1 to the total of Attack Run. '''Lore:''' “Come on, blow this big thing already and let's go back to base!” '''Comparison with the English printing:''' Printed title is 邪魔者は片づいたぞ！ (the obstruction is cleared). The Japanese numbers the two options.

Title

貴様の失策につきあうのもこれが最後だ

Card Text

場にベイダーが出ている場合に、相手が戦闘を宣言した直後に使用する。戦闘に参加している運命数＜6の相手のリーダーを目標とする。相手が戦闘に勝利しなかったなら、目標は没収値＝0となり、即座にロストする。オゼルであれば除外カードとなる。[[:File:Japanese-Hoth-You-Have-Failed-Me-For-The-Last-Time-PSA-85187828.jpg|Original Japanese printed face]].

Lore

''「ベイダー卿。艦隊は光速を脱し、これより……うわっ……うぐ……ぐえっ」''

Translation of Japanese Text

'''Title:''' You Have Failed Me For The Last Time. '''Card text:''' If Vader is on table, play just after the opponent declares a battle. Target an opponent's leader in that battle with destiny less than 6. If the opponent did not win, the target's forfeit becomes 0 and it is immediately lost. If it is Ozzel, it becomes an excluded card. '''Lore:''' Lord Vader. The fleet has left lightspeed, and from now... whoa... ugh... gueh. '''Comparison with the English printing:''' Title is a translated movie line, not a literal English title.

Notes

Japanese-language printing of [[You Have Failed Me For The Last Time]] in [[Hoth (Japanese)]].[https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf SWCCG Collecting Encyclopedia 3.2], pp. 43, 103. Title

おまえはダゴバ星系に行くのだ

Card Text

自分の支配フェイズに２フォース消費して[Hoth]がついた自分の任意の能力値＞1のキャラクターを1人、自分の人員がいる[Dagobah]がついたロケーションに移動させる。ダゴバの位置に移動させるなら、移動にはフォースを消費せず、そこに人員がいる必要もない。[[:File:Japanese-Hoth-You-Will-Go-To-The-Dagobah-System-PSA-93899917.jpg|Original Japanese printed face]].

Lore

''「そこでお前はヨーダから学ぶ。私の師たるジェダイ・マスターだ」''

Translation of Japanese Text

'''Title:''' You Will Go To The Dagobah System. '''Card text:''' During your control phase, use 2 Force to move one of your [Hoth] characters of ability greater than 1 to a [Dagobah] location where you have presence. If moving to a Dagobah location, the move costs no Force and does not need presence. '''Lore:''' There you will learn from Yoda. He is the Jedi Master who taught me. '''Comparison with the English printing:''' Paid move costs 2 Force; English costs 1 Force.

操縦する宇宙船の戦闘力に２を加える。ローグ２を操縦するなら回避値に３を加え、戦闘運命数を引けない場合にも１枚引ける。[[:File:Japanese-Hoth-Zev-Senesca-PSA-85187817.jpg|Original Japanese printed face]].

''ベスティーン星系に近いケスティック・ステーションの出身。あらゆる機種を乗りこなす温和なパイロット。ホスの氷原でルークとハンを発見した。ホスの戦いではローグ2を操縦。''
